paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: a billing and posting clerk is not the person who keeps the books, but an accounting position that verifies and records bills and other numerical data according to document evidence and billing standards and can be reviewed: verify the accuracy of billing data and correct errors, prepare itemized statements and bills or invoices for services or goods delivered or shipped and record the amounts due, keep records of invoices and supporting documents, operate typing and calculating and invoicing equipment, prepare billing documents and credit memos, handle administrative matters such as answering telephones and ordering supplies, and complete reconciliation of bank statements and paid checks and accumulation of work hours and amounts by project to compute charges and posting and other bookkeeping work; people who only want the numbers to match and are unwilling to trace the document basis, unwilling to review source documents according to the nationally unified accounting system, and unwilling to keep differences and corrections as reviewable records are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to trace every number back to its source document and check it item by item; you can sit at a desk for long periods processing tables and documents and keep the details consistent; when you find vouchers that are inaccurately or incompletely recorded you are willing to return them or ask for a correction or supplement rather than changing the numbers yourself; you are willing to stop and report situations where the accounts and the physical assets, or the accounts and the vouchers, or the accounts and each other, or the accounts and the statements do not agree.

Conditions for pausing your investment first: you have not yet completed, under any supervised condition, a full closed loop of obtaining and reviewing source documents, preparing bookkeeping vouchers, recording in the books, preparing bills or statements, and checking differences and leaving a trail, or you can only explain your interest by knowing how to keep books; nor should you treat familiarity with a particular software package or short-term data-entry speed as proof that you can independently determine billing standards or independently handle billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing matters. The document basis and bookkeeping entries, the issuance and obtaining and safekeeping of invoices, the handling of customer billing information, and billing standards and adjustment authority must be carried out in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and employer systems and must leave a traceable record; this page does not provide any accounting method, invoicing method or practice for circumventing regulation.

Occupational identity and scope must be checked separately: O*NET lists 43-3021.00 (Billing and Posting Clerks) as Job Zone 1 to 2 (SVP below 6.0), with an educational composition of 33% requiring a bachelor's degree, 25% requiring a high school diploma or equivalent, and 22% requiring an associate's or other two-year degree (the page lists only these three items); the interest code is C (Conventional). The page does not mark this occupation as Bright Outlook, and the employment projection is little or no change (the employment trends page gives 429,800 people in 2024 falling to about 427,900 in 2034, 0%, while still projecting about 42,200 openings per year on average over the projection period). At the same time it must be noted: the wage and employment and industry data on this page are all reported on a standalone basis for this occupation on the O*NET page (the page contains no Wage data for ... or Employment data for ... labels taken from other occupations). Education, vocational training, industry certification, employer hiring and position authorization, and the requirements of the applicable jurisdiction for voucher review and bookkeeping entries and invoice issuance are different states and must be verified item by item according to employer and position and jurisdiction; none of them can be automatically inferred from another.

One sentence: this is an accounting position that checks item by item against document evidence and billing standards and delivers steadily through repeated checking of large numbers of documents and tables; the core is bill preparation and posting and books and vouchers and reconciliation and error handling, not the imagination of numbers; its U.S. wages and employment are reported on a standalone basis for this occupation, and the employment projection is little or no change; on the mainland China side no precise occupational wage entry has been obtained, and this page does not fill it in with industry averages or U.S. data.

Billing and posting clerks collect, compute and record bills and accounting and other numerical data for billing purposes as authorized, and prepare bills for the delivery of services or goods. The U.S. O*NET core includes checking billing data, preparing itemized bills and recording amounts due, keeping supporting records, using office equipment and contacting customers; the position may also do professional-services time billing, reconciliation and some bookkeeping. It does not equal having full authority over accounting policy, approvals, invoicing adjustments or collection negotiation; accounting, invoice and information rules in China apply separately according to actual duties.

entries: Obtain and review vouchers | Give every number a basis | Collect source documents by business, check the completeness of the elements and approvals and authorization, and handle vouchers that are untrue or illegal or inaccurately or incompletely recorded according to procedure rather than changing the numbers yourself.

Account for and prepare bills | Make the billing standard clear | Compute amounts according to the contract or rate or procedure, prepare itemized statements and bills or invoices and record the amounts due, and keep the calculation process together with its basis.

Record in the books and post | Make the records traceable | Record in the books on the basis of reviewed accounting vouchers, register in the order of consecutively numbered pages and complete posting, and when correcting a record seal the correction point according to procedure to leave a trace.

Reconcile and handle differences | Make the accounts agree with reality | Periodically check the book records against physical assets and funds and related materials to ensure that the accounts agree with reality and with vouchers and with each other and with statements, and when a difference is found suspend it first, then establish the cause and record the disposition.

Files and safekeeping | Make the materials reviewable | Store and keep invoices and vouchers and book materials according to procedure, keep consecutive numbering and retrieval usable, manage them according to retention period requirements, and allow access according to authority.

Reporting and escalation | Make responsibility transferable | When vouchers are non-compliant or a difference cannot be explained or billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing standards are involved, report and hand over according to the authorization chain and record truthfully, without making commitments or adjustments on your own.

paragraphs: All six directions share a foundation of data and vouchers and records and compliance common sense, but the core objects, delivery results, external authority and authorization requirements differ; the same accounting or clerical experience cannot be directly converted into the authorization or decision authority of another direction (for example, whether external communication is required and whether the work directly involves statement preparation differ considerably), and this page only compares the differences in duties under public scope.

The basis for comparison is the official occupation description of O*NET 43-3021.00 and the list of related occupations on the O*NET page, as well as the adjacent occupation relationships noted in the routing materials; an adjacent relationship only indicates proximity of duties and does not mean that qualifications, authorization or positions are interchangeable.

The table below compares billing and posting clerks with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice suits each preference.

Bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks take on more complete bookkeeping and reporting and audit support and account adjustments, and usually participate directly in statement preparation; billing and posting clerks focus on the accounting and recording of bills and vouchers and billing standards, and handle only the accounts related to bills and amounts due.

If you would rather do bookkeeping and reporting and audit support, compare bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks first; if you would rather do the accounting and recording of bills and billing standards, then billing and posting clerks suit you.
Complete books and vouchers and statements and adjustments, with outputs mainly in books and statements and vouchers.
Billing and posting clerks and bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks

Bill and account collectors contact customers who owe money after a loan is made or a bill is issued and negotiate repayment and record receipts, focusing on external communication; billing and posting clerks focus on bills and vouchers and bookkeeping entries and usually do not take on external collections and payment negotiation.

If you would rather communicate directly with customers who owe money and negotiate repayment, compare bill and account collectors first; if you would rather do the checking and recording of vouchers and books and bills, then billing and posting clerks suit you.
Complete account collection and repayment recording, with outputs mainly in contact and repayment and recording records.
Billing and posting clerks and bill and account collectors

Payroll and timekeeping clerks handle work hours and attendance and payroll calculation and personal income tax and social insurance related data, with concentrated rules and a strong periodic rhythm; billing and posting clerks handle bills and amounts due and billing standards, and the object is the bills of customers or projects rather than employee compensation.

If you would rather do work-hour and payroll rules and periodic accounting, compare payroll and timekeeping clerks first; if you would rather do the accounting of customer or project bills and amounts due, then billing and posting clerks suit you.
Complete work-hour and payroll calculation and related reports, with outputs mainly in payroll ledgers and reports.
Billing and posting clerks and payroll and timekeeping clerks

Order clerks handle order intake and entry and fulfillment tracking and delivery coordination, with the rhythm driven by customer ordering and delivery milestones; billing and posting clerks handle the billing and invoicing and posting after the order, staying closer to vouchers and books.

If you would rather do order intake and fulfillment tracking, compare order clerks first; if you would rather do billing and invoicing and bookkeeping entries, then billing and posting clerks suit you.

Office clerks take on broader general administrative and clerical and reception and filing matters, with less professional depth; billing and posting clerks require higher accuracy and awareness of evidence on bills and vouchers and books.

Measures for the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China (full text of the 2023 revision)

paragraphs: Boundary: this section describes occupational risk and boundary management, not an evaluation of an individual or an employer; the document basis and bookkeeping entries, the issuance and obtaining and safekeeping of invoices, the handling of customer billing and payment information, and the authorized scope of billing standards and billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs are determined by the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and employer systems. This page is compiled on the basis of the official responsibility and task and work context fields of O*NET 43-3021.00, as well as the Accounting Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 amendment), the Measures for the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 764), and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests; it only cites the scope of application and boundaries of conduct and does not provide any accounting method or invoicing method. Accounting matters handled by units in mainland China are subject to the Accounting Law; under Article 14 the body reviewing source vouchers is the accounting body and accounting personnel, and it cannot be presumed from an English position title that all personnel have accounting review authority. Article 15 requires entries to be based on reviewed vouchers, and the requirements for consecutive paper page numbers and sealing must be distinguished from the provisions on registering and correcting electronic books under the unified accounting system; under Article 27, when accounts do not agree those with authority handle it promptly and those without authority report immediately, and it is not the case that all differences are uniformly beyond one's authority to adjust. Under Article 35, cashiers must not concurrently serve as the listed auditor, file keeper, or recorder of income and expenditure and expense and claims and debt accounts. The full text of China's Measures for the Administration of Invoices as revised in 2023: Article 3 gives electronic and paper invoices equal legal effect; Article 21 requires truthful issuance and prohibits false issuance, and the special invoice seal requirement is expressly directed at paper invoices; Article 23 also prohibits stealing, intercepting, tampering with, selling or leaking invoice data; Article 28 requires the stub copy of issued invoices to be kept for 5 years, and this cannot be used to uniformly set 5 years for all electronic invoices, accounting files and customer materials.

Direct answer: key risks include errors in billing standards and document basis, account differences and duplicate payments and missed entries, leakage of customer and billing information, long hours at a desk and repetitive actions and eye strain, loss of control over vouchers and books and invoicing records, and unclear authorization for billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing; the control approach is to obtain and review vouchers first, record according to the nationally unified accounting system and institutional procedures, correct according to procedure and leave a trail, check periodically to ensure that the accounts agree with reality and with vouchers and with each other and with statements, handle customer information on the principle of minimum necessity, and stop and escalate when beyond authorization.

Evidence scope: the risk and boundary entries are based on the official tasks of O*NET 43-3021.00 (verifying the accuracy of billing data and correcting errors, preparing itemized statements and bills or invoices and recording amounts due, keeping records of invoices and supporting documents, resolving differences in accounting records, reconciling bank statements with paid checks and adjusting differences, verifying check signatures and required information) and work context fields (93% sit continuously or almost continuously, 88% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 73% use email every day, 58% have telephone conversations every day, 56% are in contact with others continuously, 33% do repetitive actions continuously or almost continuously, 58% work indoors in an environmentally controlled setting every day, 28% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day, 16% face unpleasant or angry or impolite people more than once a week, 30% consider the consequences of error serious and 50% consider them fairly serious), as well as the provisions of the Accounting Law of the People's Republic of China on voucher review and bookkeeping entries and agreement between accounts and reality and vouchers and each other and statements and internal checks, and the provisions of the Measures for the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China on issuing and obtaining and safekeeping invoices and prohibiting false issuance and prohibiting the substitution of other vouchers for invoices.
Customers or projects and their business-side staff, as well as the person themselves and the employer

Errors in billing standards or the document basis lead to incorrect invoicing and incorrect entries, causing customer disputes and returned bills and rework of accounts, and in serious cases may affect the truthfulness and completeness of financial data.

Editorial risk checking suggestions: determine billing standards according to the contract or rate and procedure and keep the basis; do not accept untrue or illegal source vouchers and report them to the person in charge of the unit, and return inaccurately or incompletely recorded ones and require correction or supplementation; do not alter source vouchers or adjust numbers on your own; stop and escalate first when the scope is unclear or beyond authorization, and keep the calculation process and review trails.
Adjusting the numbers first and adding the basis later to meet a milestone, determining billing standards on the basis of verbal statements, or altering source vouchers and book records on your own.
The person themselves and colleagues in the same group and the chief accountant

If account differences and duplicate payments and missed entries are not established and recorded in time, they cause disagreement between accounts and reality and wrongful payments and missed receipts, and make subsequent reconciliation and closing rest on an incorrect basis.

Editorial risk checking suggestions: periodically check the accounting book records against physical assets and funds and related materials to ensure that the accounts agree with reality and with vouchers and with each other and with statements; when a difference is found suspend it first, then establish the cause and record the disposition; record and track exceptions such as returned vouchers and checks or stop payments according to procedure; make corrections using the method prescribed by the nationally unified accounting system and stamp the correction point.
Continuing to make entries or close the books before the cause of a difference is established, or making adjustments from memory without leaving a basis.
Customers and their business-side staff, as well as the person themselves and the employer

Customer billing information and payment information and transaction details may leak during handling and transmission and storage, be used for harassment or fraud, and may violate personal information protection and consumer rights protection requirements.

Editorial information protection suggestions: handle materials through institution-approved systems, channels and access scopes, and when a leak is suspected pause the questionable transmission and hand it to the information officer for determination, with recovery conditions confirmed by the institution. No employer SOP was obtained in this round, and the law does not generally prohibit all use of private devices or social software. China's Personal Information Protection Law applies to the processing of information of natural persons within the territory and other statutory situations, requiring legality, necessity and security measures; medical health and financial accounts and the like are sensitive personal information and require a specific purpose, sufficient necessity and strict protection, and the specific notice, consent and exceptions must be verified against the applicable provisions. Not all billing fields are automatically sensitive, and this cannot replace U.S. medical context requirements.

Taking customer or billing details out of the authorized system, discussing specific customer debts or amounts in public, or leaving voucher and book materials lying around without access restrictions.

Arrange ergonomic workstations and seating and monitor height and lighting and keyboard and mouse, rotate postures and arrange breaks and distance viewing and movement, process large batches of checking tasks in segments with self-check points, and report persistent discomfort early.

Pushing through sustained overtime and intense eye use, working consecutive overtime hours to meet closing deadlines, or letting visual and neck and shoulder discomfort accumulate to the point of affecting checking accuracy.

Losing control of vouchers and books and invoicing records causes unclear responsibility and basis and difficulty of tracing, and makes it impossible to demonstrate compliance in internal review and external inspection.

Editorial risk checking suggestions: keep voucher and book and billing and reconciliation and correction records according to institutional procedures, truthfully record the time and operator and basis and manual modification traces, keep consecutive numbering and retrieval usable, and manage them according to retention period requirements and access authority.
Keeping no records, or recording after the fact without time and personnel and basis, or deleting or modifying registered book records without authorization.

Unclear authorization for billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing standards may lead to commitments beyond authority or failures to escalate when required, damaging both customer rights and accounting data.

Editorial risk checking suggestions: carry out billing and invoicing related dispositions according to the institution's authorization chain; this occupation is in O*NET Job Zone 1 to 2 and the related experience requirement ranges from almost none to one year, so onboarding training and the boundaries of billing standards and adjustment and invoicing authorization especially need to be clarified at the time of hiring; matters involving invoice issuance and voiding and red-ink reversal and safekeeping, and the handling of disagreement between accounts and reality or vouchers or each other or statements, must be carried out in accordance with the nationally unified accounting system and invoice administration and institutional rules, retaining review and escalation mechanisms and reporting hazards according to procedure.

entries.answer: Compile and record bills and other numerical data for billing purposes: verify the accuracy of billing data and correct errors, prepare itemized statements and bills or invoices for services rendered or for goods delivered or shipped and record amounts due, keep records of invoices and supporting documents, operate typing and adding and calculating or invoicing equipment, prepare billing documents and shipping labels and credit memos or credit forms, and handle general administrative matters such as answering telephones and scheduling appointments and ordering supplies, and contact customers to obtain or relay account information; and within the scope of the position, review cost and revenue data to determine rates, insert statements or paid checks or letters into equipment or by hand for mailing to customers, accumulate work hours and amounts by customer or project to compute professional service charges, review purchase orders and sales slips or charge slips or hospital records to compute amounts due, resolve differences in accounting records, compute credit terms and discounts and shipping charges or rates, complete posting and other bookkeeping work, reconcile bank statements with paid checks and adjust differences, and log stop-payment notices and verify check signatures and required information.
entries.question: What does a billing and posting clerk do every day?

entries.answer: Key risks include errors in billing standards and document basis, account differences and duplicate payments and missed entries, leakage of customer and billing information, long hours at a desk and repetitive actions and eye strain, loss of control over vouchers and books and invoicing records, and unclear authorization for billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing; the control approach is to obtain and review source vouchers first, record according to the nationally unified accounting system and institutional procedures and correct according to procedure and leave a trail, check periodically to ensure that the accounts agree with reality and with vouchers and with each other and with statements, handle customer and billing information on the principles of legality and propriety and necessity, and stop and escalate when beyond authorization.
entries.question: What risk does this job most need to note in advance?

entries.answer: Look at reviewable output: whether you can review source vouchers item by item according to procedure and check the completeness of elements and approvals, whether you can record in the books on the basis of reviewed accounting vouchers and correct in order and leave a trail, and whether you can stop and report when inaccurately or incompletely recorded items or unexplainable differences or something beyond your authorization are found. An interest code of C and skill and knowledge scores only indicate that the direction is close and cannot replace this practical evidence.

entries.answer: AI and automation can change voucher element recognition and entry, bill and statement draft generation, rate and contract clause retrieval, reconciliation difference triage and report compilation; but the review of the authenticity and legality and element completeness of source vouchers, the determination of billing standards, the judgment of the causes of differences, and the disposition decisions on billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing standards are still borne by people. The degree of task automation does not equal a change in the number of positions; the official employment projection for this occupation is little or no change (0% for 2024 to 2034).
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: The review of the authenticity and legality of source vouchers, the determination of billing standards and the checking of the calculation process, whether bookkeeping entries and corrections comply with the nationally unified accounting system and institutional procedures, the judgment of the causes and disposition of reconciliation differences, and whether invoice issuance and voiding and red-ink reversal and safekeeping are compliant and whether prohibited situations such as false issuance or substituting other vouchers for invoices are involved must be borne by the person themselves and authorized personnel in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and institutional rules; system output can only serve as a rollback-able and reviewable assistive stage.

entries.answer: Check in six categories: education; vocational training; industry certification (the O*NET certification page lists several: in the medical service coding and billing direction, Certified Billing and Coding Specialist and Certified Coding Associate and Certified Medical Reimbursement Specialist and the AAPC series of coding certifications, in the bookkeeping direction Bookkeeping Certification, and in the software direction SAP Certified Associate - SAP Billing and Revenue Innovation Management and others); institutional pre-job training and systems and authority; the institution's internal authorization for billing standards and billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing and safekeeping; and the requirements of the applicable jurisdiction for accounting vouchers and books and invoices and customer information handling. On the U.S. side the O*NET education composition is 33% bachelor's degree, 25% high school diploma or equivalent, 22% associate's or other two-year degree (the page lists only these three items), the experience requirement for occupations in this zone ranges from almost none to one year, and on-the-job training from a few days to one year; the training page shows that no training program for this occupation is registered nationwide. None of them can be automatically inferred from another.

entries.answer: The work context shows that 93% sit continuously or almost continuously, 88% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 33% do repetitive actions continuously or almost continuously (another 26% more than half the time), 73% use email every day, 58% have telephone conversations every day, 57% have face-to-face discussions every day, 56% are in contact with others continuously, 58% work indoors in an environmentally controlled setting every day, 28% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day (45% never), 16% face unpleasant or angry or impolite people more than once a week, and 36% are in conflict situations more than once a month; long hours at a desk and high-frequency repetitive actions and eye strain require appropriate workstations and seating and monitors and lighting arrangements, and closing cycles bring a periodic increase in intensity, so persistent discomfort should be reported early. For the item bending or twisting the body the page does not give a percentage.
entries.question: What are the physical and psychological demands of this job?

entries.answer: The work context shows that 92% of typical work weeks are 40 hours and 100% are fixed schedules (established routine and fixed shifts); 47% have some freedom in determining tasks and priorities and 44% have a lot of freedom; 59% have some freedom in making decisions and 33% have a lot of freedom; 22% need to make decisions every day, indicating that the position has some autonomy within the process but must be accountable according to procedure; 70% consider the level of competition moderate and 21% consider there to be no competition at all; 30% consider the consequences of error serious and 50% consider them fairly serious; 61% consider repeating the same tasks extremely important. fermat_decision_card.title: What kind of person is suited to being a billing and posting clerk?

hero.quick_answer: Billing and posting clerks compile and record bills and other numerical data for billing purposes: verify the accuracy of billing data and correct errors, prepare itemized statements and bills or invoices for services rendered or for goods delivered or shipped and record amounts due, keep records of invoices and supporting documents, operate typing and adding and calculating or invoicing equipment, prepare billing documents and shipping labels and credit memos or credit forms, handle general administrative matters such as answering telephones and scheduling appointments and ordering supplies, and contact customers to obtain or relay account information; and within the scope of the position, review cost and revenue data to determine rates, answer questions about rates and routes or procedures, insert statements or paid checks or letters into equipment or by hand for mailing to customers, accumulate work hours and amounts by customer or project to compute professional service charges, consult rate manuals or sources such as insurance companies to determine specific charges or rules, review purchase orders and sales slips or charge slips or hospital records to compute amounts due, prepare cost element reports, resolve differences in accounting records, compute credit terms and discounts and shipping charges or rates, complete posting and other bookkeeping work, monitor equipment operation, reconcile bank statements with paid checks and adjust differences, weigh letters to determine postage and affix stamps or run them through a meter, log stop-payment notices, verify check signatures and required information and handle minor equipment jams; their work does not equal determinations of accounting policy and statement preparation and external audit, nor does it replace the regulatory requirements of the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and employers for accounting vouchers and books and invoice issuance, and it stops and escalates when source vouchers are untrue or illegal or inaccurate or incomplete, when agreement between accounts and reality or vouchers or each other or statements is broken, or when billing adjustments and refunds and write-offs and invoicing standards beyond one's authorization are involved.

subject.summary: Billing and posting clerks compile and record bills and other numerical data for billing purposes: verify the accuracy of billing data and correct errors, prepare itemized statements and bills or invoices and record the amounts due, keep records of invoices and supporting documents, operate typing and calculating and invoicing equipment, prepare billing documents and credit memos, handle general administrative matters such as answering telephones and ordering supplies, contact customers to obtain or relay account information, and within the scope of the position complete reconciliation of bank statements and paid checks, accumulation of work hours and amounts by project to compute charges, and resolution of differences in accounting records and postings and other bookkeeping work. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 43-3021.00 (Billing and Posting Clerks), which is Job Zone 1 to 2 (SVP below 6.0); the wage and employment and industry data are all reported on a standalone basis for this occupation, the O*NET page does not state that they are taken from other occupations, and this occupation is also not marked Bright Outlook; the employment projection is little or no change (the employment trends page gives 429,800 people in 2024 to about 427,900 people in 2034, 0%). On the mainland China side, this page has not obtained a public occupational wage entry precisely corresponding to this occupation, and according to the evidence standard retains the boundary that no data can be safely used, without filling it in with industry averages, U.S. data or non-transparent recruitment samples; bookkeeping and invoicing conduct in mainland China is subject to the Accounting Law of the People's Republic of China and the Measures for the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China and other provisions.
